{{Short description|Ring theory}}
In mathematics, the '''necklace ring''' is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Metropolis|last2=Rota|year=1983}} to elucidate the multiplicative properties of [[Necklace polynomial|necklace polynomials]].

==Definition==

If ''A'' is a commutative ring then the necklace ring over ''A'' consists of all infinite sequences <math>(a_1, a_2, ...)</math> of elements of ''A''. Addition in the necklace ring is given by pointwise addition of sequences. Multiplication is given by a sort of arithmetic convolution: the product of <math>(a_1, a_2, ...)</math> and <math>(b_1, b_2, ...)</math> has components
:<math>\displaystyle c_n=\sum_{[i,j]=n}(i,j)a_ib_j</math>

where <math>[i,j]</math> is the [[least common multiple]] of <math>i</math> and <math>j</math>, and <math>(i,j)</math> is their [[greatest common divisor]].

This ring structure is isomorphic to the multiplication of formal [[power series]] written in "necklace coordinates": that is, identifying an integer sequence <math>(a_1, a_2, ...)</math> with the power series <math>\textstyle\prod_{n\geq 0} (1{-}t^n)^{-a_n}</math>.
